result:
`bun run typecheck` and `bun test` both pass (5 tests, 0 failures).

The gap was in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:99` — `destroy()` looked the post up and deleted it without ever consulting the gate, while `update()`/`edit()` both call `this.authorize('update', [Post, post])`. `PostPolicy.delete` already existed and correctly restricts deletion to the author, so the fix is a single missing call: `destroy()` now does `await this.authorize('delete', [Post, post])` between `findOrFail` and `Post.delete`, matching the shape of the update actions — a signed-in non-author gets a 403 from the gate, guests are still handled by the `auth` middleware on the route (redirect to `/login`), and the author's own delete is unaffected. I also added `tests/PostDestroy.test.ts`, a feature test that drives the real `DELETE /posts/:id` route with `TestApp` + `withCsrf()`, asserting the non-author gets 403 and the post survives, a guest is refused and the post survives, and the author's delete redirects to `/posts` with the row gone; it creates its fixtures through the models and cleans them out of the shared test SQLite file in `afterAll`. No UI change was needed — `resources/js/pages/posts/Show.tsx` already hid the Delete button from non-authors.
